mainTopic: Which blood counts as 'blood' for הכשר (making food susceptible to טומאה), and whether the טומאה of sacrificial blood is דאורייתא or דרבנן
overview: The amud finishes a rule: only blood 'poured out like water' is מכשיר, so sacrificial blood caught for the מזבח is not. רב שמואל בר אמי challenges this from דם התמצית, which is poured like water yet is not מכשיר. רבי זירא answers that דם התמצית is not מכשיר even in חולין, because it does not count as 'blood' at all. רב שמואל בר אמי accepts this and supports it from 'כי הדם הוא הנפש': only blood that takes out the life is called דם. The גמרא then tries several proofs that sacrificial blood can become טמא מדאורייתא: a ברייתא about impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח, and a משנה about the ציץ. Both are pushed off as rabbinic טומאה that does not follow רבי יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה. A ברייתא on 'ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים' shows that the ציץ atones for טומאה, but רב פפא says it means impure קמצים, not blood. The amud ends by opening a new proof from the prophet חגי's question to the כהנים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blood not poured like water does not make food susceptible
steps.stepSummary: The second half of a derived rule: blood that is not 'poured out like water' is not מכשיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that is not poured out like water does not make food susceptible to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule that comes from the פסוק 'על הארץ תשפכנו כמים'. Blood poured out like water is מכשיר, but blood that is not poured out like water is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of קדשים is caught in a כלי and sprinkled on the מזבח, so it is not 'poured out like water'. That is why it does not give food a הכשר. The rule is based on how the blood is treated: spilled out like water, or collected for a holy use.

keyTerms.meaning: blood (one of the seven liquids that can give a הכשר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'מכשיר' here with כשר. It means making food able to become טמא, not making it fit to eat.

phrases.english: Blood that is not poured out like water
phrases.notes: For example, sacrificial blood collected for the altar.

phrases.english: does not render produce susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּם שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִשְׁפָּךְ כַּמַּיִם — אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation earlier ('poured like water' is מכשיר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood not poured out like water (sacrificial blood) is not מכשיר.

steps.title: Challenge from oozing blood
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אמי points to דם התמצית: it is poured like water, yet it is not מכשיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אמי objected: But there is oozing blood, which is poured out like water, and it still does not make food susceptible!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר אמי attacks the rule. He gives a case where blood IS poured like water but still is NOT מכשיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule implied that being 'poured like water' is the test for הכשר. דם התמצית, the blood that oozes out after the main spurt, is not fit for the מזבח and is just poured out. So by the rule it should be מכשיר, but it is not. The test seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: blood that oozes out after the main spurt of slaughter

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Ami strongly objected to it:
There is the blood squeezed out after the main spurt
which is poured out like water,
and yet it does not render produce susceptible!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'poured like water' test from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that blood poured like water is מכשיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: דם התמצית meets the 'poured like water' condition but is not מכשיר.

steps.title: Oozing blood is a separate exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that דם התמצית is no proof, because it is not מכשיר even in חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Leave aside oozing blood, since even in non-sacred animals it does not make food susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the rule. He says דם התמצית is a special case and tells us nothing about the 'poured like water' test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דם התמצית is not מכשיר even in an ordinary חולין animal, so it fails for a completely different reason. For הכשר it does not count as 'blood' at all. The 'poured like water' rule only sorts real blood, and דם התמצית never enters the picture.

keyTerms.meaning: leave aside; that case does not count

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Leave aside the oozing blood,
for even in non-sacred animals it also does not render produce susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: הַנַּח לְדַם הַתַּמְצִית
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the counter-example belongs to a different category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דם התמצית breaks the 'poured like water' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: דם התמצית is not considered blood for הכשר at all, even in חולין, so the rule stands.

steps.title: Accepted, with a verse as support
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אמי accepts the answer and supports it from 'כי הדם הוא הנפש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אמי accepted it from him, for the תורה says: 'Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the soul.' Blood with which the soul leaves is called blood. Blood with which the soul does not leave is not called blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner agrees with רבי זירא. He brings a פסוק showing why דם התמצית is not 'blood'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'blood' with the נפש, the life force. Only blood whose flow takes the life out of the animal (the main spurt of slaughter) is called דם. דם התמצית oozes out after the animal is already dead, so it is not called דם and gives no הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: For הכשר, only דם הנפש (the life-blood that pours out at death) counts as blood. Oozing דם התמצית does not count, even in חולין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a definition of 'blood' (דם הנפש) that is used in many places in the laws of הכשר.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Ami accepted it from him,
as the Merciful One said:
"Only be strong not to eat the blood,
for the blood is the soul":

phrases.aramaic: דָּם שֶׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ יוֹצְאָה בּוֹ — קָרוּי דָּם,
phrases.english: blood with which the soul leaves is called blood;

phrases.aramaic: דָּם שֶׁאֵין הַנֶּפֶשׁ יוֹצְאָה בּוֹ — אֵינוֹ קָרוּי דָּם.
phrases.english: blood with which the soul does not leave is not called blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי, דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The questioner accepts the answer of step 3 and supports it.
steps.raayaObject: That דם התמצית is not halachically 'blood'

steps.title: Proof from impure blood sprinkled on the altar
steps.stepSummary: A תא שמע: if impure blood is sprinkled by mistake the קרבן is accepted, but if on purpose it is not. This suggests the blood's טומאה is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Blood that became impure and was sprinkled: if by mistake, the offering is accepted; if on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the bigger question of whether liquids, and sacrificial blood, become טמא מדאורייתא. It brings a ברייתא to try to prove that they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats sacrificial blood as something that can become טמא, and that טומאה affects whether the קרבן is accepted. The גמרא wants to read this as a true Torah-level טומאה in the blood, which would show that liquids become טמא מדאורייתא. The next step questions whether this טומאה is really Torah-level.

keyTerms.meaning: and he sprinkled it (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Come and hear: Blood that became impure, and he sprinkled it:
if unwittingly, it is accepted;
if intentionally, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about דם התמצית and returns to the main question about the טומאה of liquids.
steps.raayaObject: That sacrificial blood (and liquids) can become impure מדאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: impure blood sprinkled בשוגג is accepted, במזיד is not

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blood's טומאה there is only מדרבנן. That ברייתא also does not follow רבי יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is rabbinic, and it does not follow רבי יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. It says the blood there is impure only by rabbinic law, so nothing is proven about Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the טומאה is only דרבנן, refusing to accept the קרבן when sprinkled במזיד is a rabbinic penalty, not proof of Torah impurity. The גמרא admits the ברייתא does not follow רבי יוסי בן יועזר. As understood earlier in the sugya, he holds that liquids of the slaughterhouse in the מקדש do not become impure at all, not even מדרבנן.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
keyTerms.meaning: early sage who testified that the slaughterhouse liquids in the מקדש are pure

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying impure blood is fine to sprinkle. It says the impurity is real but only rabbinic, and the rabbinic penalty is why the offering is not accepted במזיד.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about impure blood proves only a rabbinic טומאה. It cannot prove that the טומאה of liquids is דאורייתא.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: This short phrase is the גמרא's whole answer, so it stands on its own.

phrases.aramaic: וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה.
phrases.english: and not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof's conclusion that the טומאה is דאורייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the blood's טומאה was Torah-level, but it may be only rabbinic, with a rabbinic penalty for doing it במזיד.

steps.title: The ציץ atones for blood that became impure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the ציץ atones for impure blood, meat, and fat. This suggests that blood can truly become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: For what does the ציץ (the כהן גדול's golden headplate) bring acceptance? For the blood, the meat, and the fat that became טמא. This is true whether it happened by mistake or on purpose, by force or by choice, and whether the קרבן belongs to one person or to the whole community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that the blood of a קרבן can become טמא. The proof is a משנה about the ציץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ is only needed when something is really טמא. The משנה lists 'הדם' as one of the things the ציץ fixes. That suggests the blood itself can become טמא, apparently on a Torah level.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden headplate worn by the כהן גדול
Brings acceptance or atonement, so the קרבן is valid
By force (beyond one's control) / by choice
An individual's קרבן / a community's קרבן

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מָה הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה
phrases.english: Come and hear: for what does the frontplate atone?
For the blood and for the meat
and for the fat that became impure
phrases.notes: This is the key point: blood is listed among the things that can become טמא.

phrases.english: whether unwittingly or intentionally
whether by force or willingly
whether for an individual or for the community

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מָה הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 5 was pushed off, a new proof is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That the blood of קדשים can become טמא, apparently מדאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the things the ציץ atones for, including 'הדם שנטמא'

steps.title: Rabbinic impurity, and not like רבי יוסי בן יועזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The blood's טומאה in that משנה is only מדרבנן, and the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The impurity there is only מדרבנן. And that משנה does not follow יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof using the same answer it gave in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ also fixes blood that is טמא only מדרבנן, so the משנה proves nothing about Torah law. Even so, the משנה clearly holds that blood can at least become טמא מדרבנן. That disagrees with רבי יוסי בן יועזר, who says this blood is fully טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not according to (the opinion of)

phrases.english: By rabbinic law
and not in accordance with (Yosef) ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name in round brackets. This sage is usually called יוסי בן יועזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, וּדְלָא כְּיוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof that the טומאה is דאורייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as talking about blood that is טמא מדרבנן, so it says nothing about Torah law.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying blood cannot become טמא at all. It only says this משנה might be talking about rabbinic טומאה. That is exactly why the משנה does not fit רבי יוסי בן יועזר, who holds the blood is completely טהור.

steps.title: New proof from the verse about אהרן bearing the sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another proof from the פסוק 'ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And אהרן shall bear the sin of the holy things.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the ציץ, and the next step will explain what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the proof will come from a פסוק, not a rabbinic source. If the פסוק shows that the ציץ atones for impure blood, that would be Torah-level טומאה. In that case the 'it's only מדרבנן' answer would no longer work.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin connected to the holy offerings

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Aaron shall bear the sin of the consecrated objects"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is שמות כח:לח, talking about the ציץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְנָשָׂא אַהֲרֹן אֶת עֲוֹן הַקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rabbinic-level answer in step 8, a Torah-level source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That the ציץ atones for Torah-level טומאה of blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים'
steps.whyThisMatters: A proof from a פסוק cannot be pushed off by saying 'it's only מדרבנן'.

steps.title: Which sin does the ציץ carry? Not פיגול and not נותר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which sin the ציץ carries away. It rules out פיגול and נותר, because פסוקים already say those cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which sin does it carry? If you say the sin of פיגול, the Torah already said 'it will not be accepted.' If you say the sin of נותר, the Torah already said 'it will not be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts narrowing down what 'the sin of the holy things' means. It crosses out options one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול and נותר cannot be the sin the ציץ fixes, because the Torah says those קרבנות are never accepted. By crossing them out, the ברייתא is building toward a different sin that the ציץ does fix. That sin is likely טומאה, which would make it a Torah-level source.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן ruined by intending to eat or offer it after its allowed time
Meat of a קרבן left over past its allowed time

phrases.english: And which sin does it bear?
If the sin of piggul
it was already stated: "it shall not be accepted"
If the sin of notar
it was already stated: "it shall not be credited"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 9 by ruling out possible meanings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sin the ציץ carries away according to the פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The next step answers this question. So far פיגול and נותר are ruled out.

steps.title: The ציץ only atones for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the ציץ only carries away the sin of טומאה, because טומאה is permitted when the ציבור brings offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ציץ only carries away the sin of impurity, since impurity was permitted, as an exception to its general rule, for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from the last step. Since פיגול and נותר are ruled out, the ציץ must atone for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה is different from פיגול and נותר. The Torah already allows communal offerings to be brought in a state of טומאה. Because טומאה can be permitted in some cases, the ציץ is able to fix it in other cases too.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of bringing an offering that is impure
Was permitted as an exception to its general rule

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: So it carries only the sin of impurity
which was permitted from its general rule for the community.
phrases.notes: Communal offerings may be brought even when the people are טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's answer to the question asked in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sin does the ציץ carry away?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the sin of טומאה, because טומאה is permitted for the ציבור.

steps.title: Does this mean impure blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the impurity the ציץ fixes is impure blood. That would prove that blood can truly become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean the impurity of blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as talking about blood that became טמא. It uses this to show that blood can become טמא by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is built on a פסוק ('ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים'), so the טומאה it describes is Torah-level. If that טומאה is the טומאה of blood, then blood can become טמא מדאורייתא. Here the 'it is only מדרבנן' answer from steps 6 and 8 cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? A formula used to propose a reading as proof

phrases.english: What, is it not the impurity of blood?
phrases.notes: With "מאי לאו" the גמרא suggests a way to read it, and often that suggestion gets turned down right after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about blood from the ברייתא's conclusion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים', which says the ציץ atones for טומאה.

steps.title: רב פפא: it means impure handfuls of flour
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof. The ברייתא may be talking about קמצים of a מנחה that became טמא, not blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: No, it means the impurity of the handfuls of flour.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes off the proof. He says the ברייתא can be explained without blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ of a מנחה does the same job that blood does for an animal offering: it makes the rest permitted to the כהנים. So the ציץ fixing impurity can refer to an impure קומץ. The ברייתא no longer proves anything about blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Handfuls of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not deny that the ציץ atones for impurity. He only changes WHAT became impure: the קומץ instead of blood.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
No, it is the impurity of the handfuls.
phrases.notes: The קומץ permits the מנחה the same way blood permits an animal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא, טוּמְאַת קְמָצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 12 by giving another case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ציץ ברייתא about blood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can refer to impure קמצים, so it does not have to be about blood.

steps.title: A new proof from the question in חגי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof from the פסוק in חגי. In it, the prophet asks the כהנים about holy meat carried in a garment that touches other foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "If a person carries holy meat in the corner of his garment, and with his corner touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, does it become holy? The כהנים answered and said: No."
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a פסוק from חגי as the source for its next proof, and the explanation of how it proves the point comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a chain of contacts: holy meat, then the garment, then foods like wine and oil. Wine and oil are liquids. The גמרא will use this chain to learn about levels of טומאה, including whether liquids can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The prophet who asked this question of the כהנים

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"If a person carries holy meat
in the corner of his garment, and touches with his corner
the bread or the stew
or the wine or oil
phrases.notes: Wine and oil are liquids, which matters for the discussion.

phrases.english: or any food, does it become holy?
And the priests answered and said: No."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ציץ proof was pushed off, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether liquids such as blood can become truly טמא.
